Exodus 31:13. “Signs are physical acts that continue to be repeated in subsequent generations to confirm the existence of the covenant. One example of a sign of a covenant is the rainbow provided by God inGenesis 9:12–16. … The sign that God enjoined Abraham and his descendants to make is that of circumcision (Genesis 17:9–10, 13–14), while the sign of the Mosaic covenant was the keeping of the Sabbath day” (Hopkin, “Covenant Among Covenants,” 227).

At Sinai, the Lord made a covenant with the Israelites collectively (seeExodus 19:8). This was a common pattern in both the Old Testament and the Book of Mormon (see Kerry Muhlestein, “Covenantal Command: Love Thy Neighbor,” inCovenant of Compassion: Caring for the Marginalized and Disadvantaged in the Old Testament, ed. Avram R. Shannon and others [2021], 59). President Russell M. Nelson taught that in our day, “we travel the covenant path both individually and collectively” (“The Everlasting Covenant,”Liahona, Oct. 2022, 9).

The King James Version ofExodus 32:14states that “the Lord repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.” The Joseph Smith Translation of this verse includes the following adjustment: “And the Lord said unto Moses, If they will repent of the evil which they have done, I will spare them, and turn away my fierce wrath (Joseph Smith Translation, Exodus 32:14, Gospel Library). See also “Genesis 6:6. What are we to understand from the phrase ‘it repented the Lord’?”
